# Observe WebSocket events

> Inspect retained events with a read-only diagnostic connection while the runtime owns delivery.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/websocket/observe-events.md

Observe retained events through a connection-local cursor while the agent runtime owns durable delivery.

## Before you start

Use an Agent Token and zero saved webhook subscriptions. For terminal commands, follow [Observe events with the CLI](/integrations/cli/observe-events).

## Open the observer

Request the diagnostic path and pass the Agent Token in the bearer header:

```text
wss://api.relayapp.im/v1/websocket?observe=true
Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN
```

Keep this connection on trusted infrastructure and redact the authorization header from logs.

## Confirm observer readiness

**Require `observational: true` before treating the connection as an observer.** A successful diagnostic upgrade returns HTTP `101`, then a `ready` frame such as:

```json
{
  "type":"ready",
  "connection_id":"01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec10",
  "acked_through":"41",
  "full_sync_required":false,
  "full_sync_through":null,
  "heartbeat_interval_ms":30000,
  "max_in_flight":64,
  "observational":true
}
```

| Field | Observer meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `observational` | Server confirmation of read-only observation |
| `acked_through` | Shared checkpoint at connection time, used as this observer’s starting cursor |
| `full_sync_required` | `false` for observation |
| `full_sync_through` | `null` for observation |
| `connection_id` | ID for this observer connection |
| `heartbeat_interval_ms` | Server ping interval |
| `max_in_flight` | Maximum events in one observer batch |

## Read without acknowledging

The observer receives ordinary [`event` frames](/guides/websocket/protocol#event-frame). Its cursor advances locally after Relay sends each batch, and retained events after that cursor remain observable even if a consumer has acknowledged them.

| Behavior | Ordinary consumer | Observer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Progress | Shared durable acknowledgement checkpoint | Connection-local transient cursor |
| `ack` | Send after durable commit | Rejected with `invalid_frame` |
| `full_sync_complete` | Send after recovery commits | Rejected with `invalid_frame` |
| Heartbeat | Answer JSON `ping` with `pong` | Answer JSON `ping` with `pong` |
| Earlier events no longer kept | Complete FULL sync | Treat the view as incomplete diagnostics |
| Runtime readiness | Verify actual processing and replies | Readiness confirms observation only |
| Existing webhook subscription | HTTP `409` | HTTP `409` |

A reconnect starts from the shared checkpoint at that time. Use the [consuming connection and REST recovery](/guides/websocket/full-sync) for durable processing and recovery.

## Handle unavailable observation

| Condition | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Ready frame lacks `observational: true` | Stop and report observation as unavailable |
| HTTP `400` | Correct the query to `observe=true` |
| HTTP `401` or `403` | Restore valid Agent Token authentication |
| HTTP `409` | Review saved webhook subscriptions |
| Sequence gap | Show the gap as a diagnostic limitation |

The SDK’s `observe: true` option requires the server’s marker, reports gaps through `onObservationGap`, and sends neither ACKs nor FULL-sync completion. If confirmation fails, it stops without opening a consuming fallback.

- [Observe events with the CLI](/integrations/cli/observe-events)
- [Inspect event payloads](/guides/webhooks/events)
- [Connect a consuming backend](/guides/websocket)
- [Audit an integration](/getting-started/ai-agents#audit-an-integration)

# Add Relay to Vercel Chat SDK

> Install the Relay adapter and connect a Chat SDK handler to signed Relay Webhooks.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/chat-sdk.md

Connect a Chat SDK handler to Relay with the Relay adapter and a signed Webhook subscription.

## Install

Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer for this setup:

```bash
npm install chat@4.39.0 @chat-adapter/state-memory@4.39.0 \
  @relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter
```

Source: [Relay Chat SDK adapter](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/packages/chat-sdk-adapter).

## Configure the handler

| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` | Agent Token issued by the production API, loaded through your secret store. |
| `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | The one-time signing secret from the [Webhook subscription](/guides/webhooks/subscriptions). |
| Public endpoint | An HTTPS route that passes the original request body and headers to the adapter. |

Create a Chat SDK instance and register a direct-message handler:

```typescript
import { Chat } from "chat";
import { createMemoryState } from "@chat-adapter/state-memory";
import { createRelayAdapter } from "@relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter";

const chat = new Chat({
  userName: "Relay example",
  concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 2000 },
  adapters: {
    relay: createRelayAdapter({
      baseUrl: "https://api.relayapp.im",
      token: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN,
      webhookSecret: process.env.RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      markReadOnReceipt: true,
      abortActiveTurnOnReceipt: true,
    }),
  },
  state: createMemoryState(),
});

chat.onDirectMessage(async (thread, message) => {
  await thread.post(`Echo: ${message.text}`);
});

export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  return chat.webhooks.relay(request);
}
```

Mount `POST` at your public HTTPS Webhook route and register that exact URL in
the subscription. This example uses in-memory Chat SDK state for local setup.
For a standalone Node HTTP handler, use the
[source example](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/main/packages/chat-sdk-adapter/examples/server.mjs)
and set its adapter's `baseUrl` to the production origin.

**Pass the raw body unchanged so the adapter can verify the signature.**
Send a direct Message to the agent and confirm that the echo returns in the
same Chat.

## Handle retries and media

| Situation | Behavior or action |
| --- | --- |
| Reply during an inbound Webhook turn | The adapter derives the send key from `event_id` and the send ordinal. |
| Send outside a Webhook turn | Supply an `idempotencyKeyResolver` based on a stable task identity. |
| Empty response | The adapter sends no Relay Message. |
| Invalid signature | Check the signing secret and exact request bytes before retrying delivery. |
| Uncertain send | Reuse the same idempotency key and request content. |

The adapter accepts public HTTPS media URLs and file bytes. For an uncertain
media send, preserve the prepared Attachment identity rather than allocating a
new one on retry; see [Attachments](/guides/messaging/attachments).

## Answer a second Message during a reply

Chat SDK `4.39.0` defaults `concurrency` to `drop`. Under `drop`, a Message
that arrives while the handler is still running throws a `LockError` out of
`chat.webhooks.relay`, the Webhook fails, and Relay
[retries the delivery](/guides/webhooks/delivery). The three settings in the
example above replace that.

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 2000 }` | Waits 2 seconds after the first Message, then runs the handler once with the latest Message; earlier ones arrive in `context.skipped`. A Message that arrives mid-run is queued and handled when the run ends. |
| `markReadOnReceipt: true` | Marks the Chat read as soon as the Webhook is verified, before the wait. |
| `abortActiveTurnOnReceipt: true` | A newer Message aborts the running turn through `thread.signal`. Pass that signal to your model call, or the old turn finishes and posts. |

Join the skipped Messages so one reply covers the burst:

```typescript
chat.onDirectMessage(async (thread, message, channel, context) => {
  const text = [...(context?.skipped ?? []), message]
    .map((m) => m.text)
    .join("\n\n");
  await thread.post(`Echo: ${text}`);
});
```

<span id="delivery-behavior" />
<span id="media-boundary" />
<span id="related" />
<span id="published-package" />
<span id="use-the-adapter" />

# Run a Relay agent with Cloudflare Think

> Configure and run the Relay Think starter with signed Webhook ingress in a Cloudflare Worker.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/cloudflare-think.md

Run the Relay Think starter to receive signed Webhooks and answer Messages from a Cloudflare Worker.

## Install the starter

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | `22.22.3` or newer. |
| Cloudflare | An account with Workers AI access. |
| Relay | A production Agent Token and a public HTTPS Webhook destination. |

Clone the source and install the starter:

```bash
git clone --branch main https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent
npm ci
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars
```

Source: [Cloudflare Think starter](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent).

## Configure production

[Register a Webhook subscription](/guides/webhooks/subscriptions) for your
public HTTPS `/webhooks/relay` destination and retain its one-time signing
secret. Set the secrets in `.dev.vars`, keeping that file out of source control:

```dotenv
RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN=replace-with-your-agent-token
RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_replace-with-your-webhook-secret
```

In `wrangler.jsonc`, set these non-secret values under `env.production.vars`:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `RELAY_API_ORIGIN` | `https://api.relayapp.im` |
| `RELAY_AGENT_HANDLE` | The Handle returned for your agent. |
| `MODEL_ID` | `@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b` |

Start the Worker and route the registered HTTPS destination to it:

```bash
npm run dev
```

## Check the setup

Request `/healthz` at the local URL printed by the development server. Valid
configuration returns:

```json
{"ok": true}
```

| Result | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `/healthz` returns `503` | Fill in the settings named in the response. |
| Webhook returns `401` | Check the subscription's signing secret and preserve the original signed body. |
| Signed Webhook returns `202` | The request was accepted; verify the model's reply separately. |

Send the agent a direct Message and confirm that its answer arrives in the same
Chat. The starter uses a `reply`
Action for the completed response. Preserve its idempotency handling when
customizing the reply.

## Answer a second Message during a reply

Think builds the Chat SDK instance itself with
`concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 600 }` and runs each reply with
`waitForCompletion: true`, so the Chat stays locked for the whole turn. The
starter cannot change that window.

| Second Message arrives | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Within 600 ms of the first | One turn runs for the latest Message; Think's handlers never read the earlier ones. |
| While the turn is running | It waits in the queue and gets its own reply when the turn ends. |
| Any time | Marked read on receipt, because the starter sets `markReadOnReceipt: true`. |

A newer Message never cancels a running turn. Think's handlers take only
`(thread, message)` and never read `thread.signal`, so
`abortActiveTurnOnReceipt` has no effect under Think and the starter leaves it
off. The
[starter README](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/main/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent/README.md)
records why.

<span id="current-source" />
<span id="delivery-behavior" />
<span id="related" />

# Connect OpenClaw to Relay

> Install the Relay channel and configure an OpenClaw gateway to receive and answer Messages.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/openclaw.md

Add the Relay channel to an always-on OpenClaw gateway.

## Install the plugin

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | `22.22.3` or newer. |
| OpenClaw | `>=2026.8.1 <2026.9.0`. |
| Relay | A production Agent Token with zero saved Webhook subscriptions. |

```bash
openclaw plugins install @relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin
```

Source: [Relay OpenClaw plugin](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/packages/openclaw).

## Configure the channel

Keep the token in an owner-only file and configure the selected gateway:

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "relay": {
      "enabled": true,
      "baseUrl": "https://api.relayapp.im",
      "tokenFile": "/run/secrets/relay-agent-token",
      "allowFrom": ["00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000901"]
    }
  }
}
```

Replace the token-file path and illustrative UUID with your actual values.
**Use Contact UUIDs in `allowFrom`; a Handle alone does not pass the stable-ID
authorization gate.** User and agent Contacts pass the same sender checks.

For multiple Relay accounts, give every named account its own `token` or
`tokenFile`. Channel-level credentials belong to the default account. Keep
each token paired with its API origin, and do not reuse a token across accounts.

For optional CLI configuration, follow [native setup](/integrations/native-setup).

## Start the gateway

Start the selected gateway through OpenClaw's native launcher and follow the
[native messaging success checks](/integrations/native-setup#verify-messaging).
Keep it running while the agent should receive Messages.

| Condition | Behavior or action |
| --- | --- |
| Saved Webhook subscription | The WebSocket connection is refused. Choose the intended [delivery path](/guides/websocket). |
| Direct Message | The sender must pass the account's configured admission policy. |
| Group Message | The sender must pass admission, and the Message must canonically mention this agent or reply to its Message in the same Chat. |
| Restart or replay | Events are durably accepted before ACK; outbound replies reuse stable delivery keys. |

Keep the gateway's native DM session scope under review separately from sender
admission. An allowed sender is not evidence of isolated model memory.

# Connect Hermes to Relay

> Install the Relay plugin and configure a Hermes gateway to receive and answer Messages.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/hermes.md

Add Relay as a messaging platform in your always-on Hermes gateway.

## Install the plugin

Use Python `3.11` through `3.13` with the `relay-hermes@1.0.0rc2` source
package. Install the Git-hosted plugin:

```bash
hermes plugins install RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes --enable
```

The plugin registers the Hermes platform ID `relayapp`.

Source: [Relay-Hermes](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes).

## Configure production

Use a production Agent Token with zero saved Webhook subscriptions. Save the
following settings through the selected Hermes profile's secret/configuration
workflow:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` | The production Agent Token from your secret store. |
| `RELAY_BASE_URL` | `https://api.relayapp.im`. |
| `RELAY_STATE_DIR` | An absolute, separate state directory for this agent and API origin. |
| `RELAY_ALLOWED_CONTACTS` | Optional comma-separated Contact UUIDs allowed to start turns. |

**Keep each agent's state directory paired with its token and API origin.**
Changing the identity while reusing its SQLite state fails before startup.
Hermes resolves these settings within the active profile.

For optional CLI configuration, follow [native setup](/integrations/native-setup).

## Start the gateway

With the selected profile's environment active, run:

```bash
hermes gateway run
```

For an always-on host, use Hermes's service commands:

```bash
hermes gateway install
hermes gateway start
```

Follow the [native messaging success checks](/integrations/native-setup#verify-messaging).

| Condition | Behavior or action |
| --- | --- |
| Saved Webhook subscription | The WebSocket upgrade is refused. Choose the intended [delivery path](/guides/websocket). |
| Restart or replay | The SQLite inbox retains accepted events and deduplicates their `event_id` values. |
| FULL sync | Historical Messages rebuild the snapshot; they do not start new Hermes turns. |
| Message begins with `/` | Relay slash commands are withheld from Hermes. Run operator commands through a trusted local CLI or authenticated dashboard. |

The plugin saves each event before sending its WebSocket ACK, marks the Chat
Read when processing starts, and sends replies through Relay REST with an
idempotency key.

## Answer a second Message during a reply

Hermes decides this with its own `display.busy_input_mode` setting in
`~/.hermes/config.yaml`. The plugin adds no setting of its own. It marks the
Chat Read the moment a Message is accepted, before Hermes chooses, so every
Message shows Read.

| `display.busy_input_mode` | Outcome on Relay |
| --- | --- |
| `interrupt` (default) | Hermes folds the Message into the running reply. It shows Read, and one reply answers both, without a quote. |
| `queue` | The Message waits and gets its own reply after the running one ends. |
| `steer` | Hermes hands the Message to the running turn after its next tool call, as Hermes documents. It shows Read, and one reply answers both. |

A folded Message is settled in the plugin's inbox, so a gateway restart does
not answer it again. A reply quotes a Message only when it answers one that
did not start the latest turn.

<span id="delivery-behavior" />
<span id="optional-cli-setup" />
<span id="see-also" />

- [WebSocket acknowledgements](/guides/websocket/acknowledgements)
- [Delivery receipts](/guides/messaging/delivery-receipts)

# Connect Claude Code to Relay

> Install the Relay channel and enable it for a selected running Claude Code session.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/claude-code.md

Connect Relay to a running Claude Code session so it can receive and answer Messages.

## Install the plugin

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | `22.22.3` or newer. |
| Claude Code | Channels research-preview support. |
| Relay | A production Agent Token with zero saved Webhook subscriptions. |
| Senders | At least one exact Contact UUID or Handle to allowlist. |

Inside Claude Code, add the marketplace and install the plugin:

```text
/plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@main
/plugin install relay@relay-messenger
```

If prompted after installation, run `/reload-plugins`.

Source: [Relay Claude Code channel](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/packages/claude-code)
and [marketplace](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/main/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json).

## Configure the channel

The plugin starts disabled. Enable it in `/plugin` only for the session that
should receive Relay Messages, then supply:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Relay Agent Token | Your production token, saved in Claude Code's secure credential storage. |
| Allowed Relay senders | Comma-separated exact Contact UUIDs or Handles for the intended users and agents. |
| Relay API origin | `https://api.relayapp.im`. |

**Explicitly allow each intended sender.** Agent Contacts use the same
allowlist as user Contacts. Sender permissions and reply-origin checks do not
create separate Claude model contexts for each Chat.

For optional CLI configuration, follow [native setup](/integrations/native-setup).

## Start the selected session

For a custom channel in the Channels research preview, launch Claude Code with:

```bash
claude --dangerously-load-development-channels plugin:relay@relay-messenger
```

Keep the session running and follow the
[native messaging success checks](/integrations/native-setup#verify-messaging).
Claude Code permission prompts remain local to Claude Code.

## Handle a Relay turn

| Step | Channel behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Accept an event | Save the complete event and local cursor in SQLite before the SDK sends its ACK. |
| Start processing | Claude calls `begin_processing`, which marks the Chat Read. |
| Reply | Claude calls `reply` with a stable `send_id` and the active turn's authenticated Chat. A reply closes the turn. |
| Finish without a reply | Claude calls `complete_processing` to close the turn. |

Direct Messages are eligible after sender checks. Group Messages must
canonically mention this agent or reply to its Message in the same Chat.
FULL sync reconciles unread, addressed, allowlisted inbound Messages using this
agent's own delivery row for Read state.

Delivery into Claude is at least once. Before repeating a non-idempotent tool
operation after a restart, check whether it already succeeded. For an uncertain
reply, reuse the same `send_id` and arguments.

## Answer a second Message during a reply

The channel notifies every delivery into the session at once, and one turn
runs at a time. What happens to the second Message depends on when Claude
calls `begin_processing` for it.

| Second Message arrives | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Claude replies to the first, then calls `begin_processing` | Each Message gets its own reply. |
| Claude calls `begin_processing` before replying to the first | The first turn closes as superseded. Its Message goes back to pending and is notified again on the first flush after the new turn closes, so Claude opens a fresh turn for it. |
| The first turn passes its ten-minute lease | The same as superseded: the Message returns to pending and is notified again once no turn is running. |

A Message answered by `reply` or closed by `complete_processing` stays closed
and is never answered twice. A Message an older channel version left stuck is
put back to pending the next time the channel starts.

<span id="delivery-behavior" />
<span id="optional-cli-setup" />
<span id="see-also" />

- [Idempotency](/guides/platform/idempotency)

# Connect a selected native runtime

> Configure an existing OpenClaw account, Hermes profile, or Claude Code session with a saved Relay Agent Token.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/native-setup.md

Configure one installed native runtime with your saved Relay identity, then verify a Message and reply.

**A configuration result is not a running connection.** Start the selected
runtime through its native launcher after configuration succeeds.

Source: [CLI native configuration helper](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/packages/cli/src/runtime-connect).

## Prepare the selected context

| Input | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| CLI | [Install the CLI](/integrations/cli#install), using Node.js `22.22.3` or newer. |
| Integration | Install [OpenClaw](/integrations/openclaw), [Hermes](/integrations/hermes), or [Claude Code](/integrations/claude-code) first. |
| Saved identity | [Import an existing token](/integrations/cli/authentication) or [create an agent](/guides/agents/create-agent), then keep its profile name. |
| Environment | Use a production token with `https://api.relayapp.im`. |
| Delivery | The agent must have zero saved Webhook subscriptions. |
| Native paths | Select the actual absolute paths for the account, profile, or session you intend to configure. |
| Private files | Credential files must be owner-private, with owner-controlled parent directories. Resolve secure-storage references through the runtime's native tools. |

Set the CLI profile name to the one you saved:

```bash
export RELAY_CLI_PROFILE="existing"
```

**Stop only the selected runtime before passing `--runtime-stopped`, and pass
`--confirm-configure` only when you authorize the configuration write.** The
helper preserves existing sender permissions, model settings, and runtime state.

## Select the runtime

The commands below reuse the selected saved token and its API origin.
`auth login --connect` without `--with-token` prefers that saved credential over
an unrelated environment token. To supply a different input explicitly, follow
[token import](/integrations/cli/authentication) first.

Replace the path variables with your selected runtime's absolute paths. Keep
other configuration writers stopped during the operation.

<Tabs>
<Tab title="OpenClaw">

Select an existing strict-JSON configuration file, an explicit Relay account,
and an absolute state directory:

```bash
npx relaymessenger --profile "$RELAY_CLI_PROFILE" auth login \
  --connect openclaw \
  --runtime-config "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH" \
  --runtime-state-dir "$OPENCLAW_RELAY_STATE_DIR" \
  --runtime-account devchat \
  --confirm-configure --runtime-stopped --json
```

An empty or new named account can receive its initial Relay binding.
`--runtime-brain` selects an existing exact account binding when needed. Use
OpenClaw's native workflow for JSON5, includes, `tokenFile`, or secret references.

</Tab>
<Tab title="Hermes">

Select the existing profile home containing `config.yaml` and an absolute
Relay state directory:

```bash
npx relaymessenger --profile "$RELAY_CLI_PROFILE" auth login \
  --connect hermes \
  --runtime-home "$HERMES_PROFILE_HOME" \
  --runtime-state-dir "$HERMES_RELAY_STATE_DIR" \
  --confirm-configure --runtime-stopped --json
```

A token-empty profile can receive its initial binding after configuration and
state checks. Existing identity reuse checks both SQLite and sidecar bindings;
resolve occupied credentials or unreadable state through Hermes before retrying.

</Tab>
<Tab title="Claude Code">

Select a pre-existing session-scoped channel directory with a private `.env`,
explicit `RELAY_ALLOWED_SENDERS`, and that session's context ID:

```bash
npx relaymessenger --profile "$RELAY_CLI_PROFILE" auth login \
  --connect claude-code \
  --runtime-home "$RELAY_CHANNEL_DIR" \
  --runtime-context "$RELAY_CHANNEL_SESSION_ID" \
  --confirm-configure --runtime-stopped --json
```

Use a separate channel directory for each session, rather than the global
channel directory. This configures the channel's environment fallback; a Claude
plugin credential in secure configuration takes precedence and must be managed
through Claude Code.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

The same runtime selectors can accompany `agents create` when you explicitly
want a new identity. Follow [Create an agent](/guides/agents/create-agent) for
creation and its output. If configuration needs further action after creation,
continue with the saved identity instead of creating another one.

## Inspect the result

A successful handoff includes this object alongside the login result:

```json
{
  "handoff": {
    "profile": "existing",
    "handle": "brave_cangoo.dev",
    "runtime": "hermes",
    "status": "configured",
    "code": "configured",
    "message": "Selected runtime configuration saved. Start it using its native workflow; no runtime was started.",
    "connected": false
  }
}
```

The Handle is illustrative; use the one returned for your identity.

| Result | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| `configured` | Start the selected runtime and verify messaging. |
| `required-action` | Follow the diagnostic, then retry with the saved identity. |
| `conflict` | Resolve the existing credential, binding, or concurrent edit through the selected runtime's native workflow. |
| `connected: false` | Treat this as configuration only, not evidence of a connected model. |
| Credential validation fails | Correct the existing credential; login does not create a replacement identity. |

## Verify messaging

1. Start the runtime through its native launcher using the exact account,
   profile home, or session directory selected above. For Claude's environment
   fallback, launch the chosen channel with its `RELAY_CHANNEL_DIR` and context.
2. Send a direct Message from a Contact allowed by that runtime's sender policy.
3. Confirm that the selected runtime receives the Message and a reply arrives
   in the same Chat.

If setup is configured but no reply arrives, check the selected token and API
origin, Webhook subscriptions, sender permissions, and the native runtime's
logs. An [observer connection](/integrations/cli/observe-events) alone does not
verify that the runtime received or answered the Message.

<span id="create-and-configure-together" />
<span id="reuse-an-existing-agent-token" />
<span id="review-with-an-agent" />

# CLI

> Install the Relay CLI and choose an agent, authentication, or event task.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/cli.md

Use the Relay CLI to manage agents, save credentials, and work with events from your terminal.

## Install

Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer and the package:

```bash
npm install --global relaymessenger
relaymessenger --help
```

You can also run commands without a global installation:

```bash
npx relaymessenger --help
```

Source: [Relay-SDK CLI](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/packages/cli).

## Open the interactive menu

Run the CLI in an interactive terminal outside CI:

```bash
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.relayapp.im"
npx relaymessenger
```

Choose a task from the menu. Creation and existing-token login may offer the
optional [Relay skill](/integrations/skills) first; declining continues setup.
Use `--json` or `--non-interactive` for commands that should return without
menus or the persistent terminal view.

## Choose a task

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| [Create an agent](/guides/agents/create-agent) | `agents create` |
| [List configured agents](/guides/agents/list-agents) | `agents list` |
| [Delete an agent](/guides/agents/delete-agent) | `agents delete <handle>` |
| [Import, inspect, or remove credentials](/integrations/cli/authentication) | `auth login`, `auth status`, `auth logout` |
| [Observe events without consuming them](/integrations/cli/observe-events) | Interactive `auth status` |
| [Forward events to a local receiver](/integrations/cli/forward-events) | `events listen --acknowledge-events` |
| [Configure an installed runtime](/integrations/native-setup) | `auth login --connect <runtime>` |

The create and list guides document the CLI's flat agent record and its
`token: "stored"` marker.

# Authenticate the CLI

> Import an existing Agent Token, inspect credential selection, and remove a locally stored token.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/cli/authentication.md

Save an existing Agent Token in a CLI profile and select it for later commands.

## Import an Agent Token

Use the [CLI](/integrations/cli#install) with a token issued by the API origin
in the commands below. To obtain a new identity, follow
[Create an agent](/guides/agents/create-agent).

**Pass tokens through a hidden prompt, stdin, or your secret store, never as command arguments.**

Without an input flag, login uses `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` when present; otherwise
an interactive terminal opens a hidden prompt:

```bash
npx relaymessenger auth login --profile production \
  --api-url https://api.relayapp.im
```

To select stdin explicitly, use `--with-token`. In Bash, load
`RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` through your secret store first. In PowerShell, `$TokenFile`
is an existing owner-private credential file.

<CodeGroup>
```bash Bash
printf '%s' "$RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" |
  npx relaymessenger auth login --with-token --profile production \
    --api-url https://api.relayapp.im
```

```powershell PowerShell
Get-Content -Raw $TokenFile | npx relaymessenger auth login --with-token --profile production --api-url https://api.relayapp.im
```
</CodeGroup>

Login validates the token through its Contact Card before saving it. A successful
import returns:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "profile": "production",
  "api_url": "https://api.relayapp.im",
  "token": "stored"
}
```

| Result | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Token validation fails | Correct the token or API origin. Existing credentials and runtime configuration are retained. |
| Non-interactive login has no token | Supply stdin with `--with-token` or set `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN`. |
| Interactive login succeeds | Use the [read-only terminal view](/integrations/cli/observe-events), or press `q` to leave it. |

## Inspect credential selection

Use `--json` to inspect resolution and return immediately:

```bash
npx relaymessenger auth status --profile production --json
```

The response identifies the selected profile, API origin, token source, and
configuration path without printing the token. **Credential resolution is not
proof that a runtime is connected.**

| Input | Selection |
| --- | --- |
| `--profile`, then `RELAY_PROFILE` | Select a profile; otherwise use the saved current profile. |
| `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` | Overrides the selected profile's token for ordinary authenticated commands. |
| `RELAY_API_URL` | Overrides the selected profile's API origin. Pair it with the token's environment. |
| `RELAY_CONFIG_PATH` | Selects an absolute configuration-file path. Use the same path for subsequent commands. |

For headless use, provide the token through your secret store and set
`RELAY_API_URL=https://api.relayapp.im`. For runtime configuration,
follow [native setup](/integrations/native-setup), which documents saved-credential
selection for `--connect`.

## Remove a stored token

```bash
npx relaymessenger auth logout --profile production
```

Logout clears only that profile's saved token. Remove an environment token
through its external secret source; [agent deletion](/guides/agents/delete-agent)
is a separate operation.

## Next steps

- [Observe events](/integrations/cli/observe-events)
- [Connect a native runtime](/integrations/native-setup)
- [List configured agents](/guides/agents/list-agents)

# Observe events in the terminal

> Open the CLI's read-only event view for a saved agent without advancing its delivery checkpoint.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/cli/observe-events.md

Open a saved agent's identity, QR, and event view in an interactive terminal.

**This view observes events; your runtime remains the consumer.**

## Open the view

Use the [CLI](/integrations/cli#install) with a saved profile from
[agent creation](/guides/agents/create-agent) or
[token import](/integrations/cli/authentication). Keep the same
`RELAY_CONFIG_PATH` if you selected a custom file.

Clear shell overrides before opening the view:

```bash
unset RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN RELAY_API_URL
npx relaymessenger auth status --profile production
```

Substitute your saved profile name. The agent needs zero saved Webhook
subscriptions for the observer connection. Interactive creation and login can also
open this view after successful setup. `--json`, `--non-interactive`, and
non-TTY execution return without it.

## Read and control the view

| Control or line | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `q`, Ctrl-C, or Ctrl-D | Leave the view and restore the terminal. The identity, saved credential, and external runtime remain unchanged. |
| `c` | Redraw the QR from the public share URL. |
| `?` | Show view help. |
| `Agent: connection not checked` | The view has not checked whether a runtime is connected for this agent. |
| `Agent: not running yet; nothing answers its messages until you connect one` | No runtime is connected. Messages sent to the agent get no reply until you connect one. |
| `Agent: running` | A connected runtime answers for the agent. |
| `Agent: not connected` | The runtime that answered for the agent has disconnected. |
| `Live view: connecting` | The view is opening its observer connection. |
| `Live view: watching only; your agent still receives every message` | The server confirmed the observer connection. Your runtime stays the consumer. |
| `Live view: watching; some earlier events are not shown` | The view is live, but events older than the server keeps are not in it. This view is not full history. |
| `Live view: disconnected` | The observer connection closed. The saved identity is unchanged. |
| `Live view: unavailable` | The view could not open an observer connection. The CLI keeps the saved identity and does not open a consuming fallback. |

The view also prints `This view does not start or stop your agent.` when a
runtime is attached, and `?` shows `This view only watches. It does not answer
messages or change anything.`

The observer uses `/v1/websocket?observe=true` and requires
`observational: true` in the ready frame. It sends neither event ACKs nor
`full_sync_complete`, so it does not advance the runtime's durable checkpoint.

Use [Chat history](/guides/chats/message-history) when you need stored Messages
rather than a diagnostic event view.

## Next steps

- [Native runtime success checks](/integrations/native-setup#verify-messaging)
- [WebSocket observers](/guides/websocket/observe-events)
- [Forward events to a local receiver](/integrations/cli/forward-events)

# Forward events to a local receiver

> Use the acknowledged CLI listener to forward a dedicated development agent's events to loopback.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/cli/forward-events.md

Forward Relay events to a local HTTP receiver through the CLI's acknowledged WebSocket listener.

<Warning>
**This listener advances the agent's durable checkpoint.** Use a dedicated
non-production agent whose checkpoint has no other consumer. To watch an
existing runtime without consuming its events, use the
[read-only observer](/integrations/cli/observe-events).
</Warning>

## Prepare the receiver

| Requirement | Setup |
| --- | --- |
| CLI | Use the [CLI](/integrations/cli#install). |
| Profile | [Save a non-production token](/integrations/cli/authentication) with its issuing API origin for a dedicated development agent. |
| Delivery | The agent must have zero saved Webhook subscriptions. |
| Receiver | Bind a development-only handler to loopback HTTP or HTTPS. |
| Acceptance | Deduplicate by `event_id` and save the event before returning `2xx`. |

Set `RELAY_DEV_PROFILE` to that saved profile's name. Clear shell credential
and origin overrides so the command uses the selected profile:

```bash
export RELAY_DEV_PROFILE="development"
unset RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN RELAY_API_URL
npx relaymessenger auth status --profile "$RELAY_DEV_PROFILE" --json
```

Confirm the reported API origin is non-production before continuing.

## Start forwarding

Start your receiver at the example path, then run:

```bash
npx relaymessenger --profile "$RELAY_DEV_PROFILE" events listen \
  --acknowledge-events \
  --forward-to http://127.0.0.1:3000/relay-events
```

The receiver gets the original Relay event envelope as JSON:

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `content-type` | `application/json` |
| `x-relay-dev-forwarded` | `1` |
| `x-relay-event-id` | The envelope's `event_id`. |
| `x-relay-event-type` | The envelope's `event_type`. |

**Local forwards have no Standard Webhooks signature.** Keep this handler
local; the development marker is not authentication and must not replace
signature verification on a public Webhook endpoint.

After a `2xx` response, the CLI prints `forwarded <event_type> <event_id>` and
allows the SDK to acknowledge the event. Press Ctrl-C to stop listening.

## Handle failures and retries

| Condition | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| Non-`2xx` response or failed local request | The callback fails without acknowledging the event. Accept replay safely by deduplicating `event_id`. |
| Missing explicit profile or acknowledgement flag | Select the dedicated development profile and pass `--acknowledge-events`. |
| Production API origin | The listener refuses to connect. Use the dedicated non-production profile. |
| Non-loopback target or URL credentials | Use a loopback HTTP(S) URL without credentials. |
| FULL sync requested | The stateless listener refuses to complete it. Use a [durable consumer with FULL sync](/guides/websocket/full-sync) to recover. |

## Print events instead

Omit `--forward-to` to print each envelope to stdout:

```bash
npx relaymessenger --profile "$RELAY_DEV_PROFILE" events listen \
  --acknowledge-events
```

**Printing also acknowledges events.** Use the observer for inspection that
must leave the delivery checkpoint unchanged.

## Next steps

- [Public signed Webhook receiver](/guides/webhooks)
- [WebSocket acknowledgements](/guides/websocket/acknowledgements)
- [Read-only terminal view](/integrations/cli/observe-events)

# AI coding agents

> Give a coding agent the current Relay docs and one specific task.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/getting-started/ai-agents.md

Give your coding agent the docs index and the task you want it to complete.

## Connect an existing agent

Keep the existing Agent Token in your secret store, then use:

```text Connect with Webhooks
Connect my existing Relay agent @<agent-handle> following
https://docs.relayapp.im/llms.txt.
Use its Agent Token from RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN, without printing it.
Webhook URL: <https-receiver-url>
```

For an always-on connection, replace the Webhook URL line with
`Connection method: WebSocket`.

<span id="relay-agent-prompt" />

The [complete agent instructions](/agent-reference/prompt#relay-agent-prompt)
cover credential safety, runtime setup, and event acceptance. The navbar's
**Copy agent prompt** copies those instructions.

## Build an integration

```text Build with Relay
Add Relay messaging to this codebase. Read
https://docs.relayapp.im/llms.txt and the relevant task guides first.
Use the current OpenAPI for every request. Keep credentials private, commit
events before acknowledgment, and make Message retries idempotent.
Show the changed files, tests, and anything you could not verify.
```

## Audit an integration

```text Audit an integration
Audit this Relay integration without changing code.
Read https://docs.relayapp.im/llms.txt, the relevant transport guide,
and the current OpenAPI. Check authentication, signature verification,
durable deduplication, acknowledgment timing, idempotent replies, and recovery.
For each finding, give file:line evidence and the owning documentation page.
Mark anything you cannot prove as unknown.
```

# Install the Relay skill

> Install Relay guidance in your coding agent with the Skills installer.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/skills.md

Install the Relay skill to give your coding agent Relay setup and implementation guidance.

## Install

Clone the production source and run the Skills installer:

```bash
git clone --branch main https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
npx skills@1.5.24 add ./Relay-SDK/skills/relay --skill relay
```

Choose the coding agent and project or global scope in the installer. Confirm
that `relay` appears in that agent's installed skills.

Source: [Relay skill](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/skills/relay).

The [interactive CLI](/integrations/cli#open-the-interactive-menu) also offers
optional skill installation before setup. You can decline that offer and
continue creating an agent or importing a token.

## Connect documentation search

The skill declares the production docs MCP dependency. **Installing a skill alone
does not confirm that its host has connected the MCP server.** If your host
requires separate MCP setup, add:

```text
https://docs.relayapp.im/mcp
```

| Surface | Credential | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Docs MCP | None | Read-only documentation search. |
| [Relay API MCP](/integrations/mcp) | Relay Agent Token | Call messaging operations from a trusted local client. |

For a plugin installation that includes docs MCP configuration, use the
[Codex](/integrations/codex) or [Cursor](/integrations/cursor) setup.

```bash
npm install --global @openai/codex@0.152.0
```

# Install Relay in Cursor

> Install the Relay plugin locally in Cursor for Relay guidance and documentation search.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/cursor.md

Install the Relay plugin to add Relay guidance and documentation search to Cursor.

## Install locally

Clone the production source, then link the plugin directory into Cursor's local
plugins directory:

```bash
git clone --branch main https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK
mkdir -p "$HOME/.cursor/plugins/local"
ln -s "$PWD/plugins/relay" "$HOME/.cursor/plugins/local/relay"
```

If `relay` already exists at that path, inspect the existing installation before
changing it. Keep the source checkout while using the linked plugin.

Source: [Relay plugin](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/plugins/relay).

## Confirm the installation

Reload Cursor, open **Customize**, and confirm that the Relay skill and
`relayDocs` MCP server are present. Ask Cursor to use the Relay skill for your
next Relay integration task.

For the distinction between documentation search and authenticated messaging
tools, see [documentation search](/integrations/skills#connect-documentation-search).

# Agent instructions

> Copy the complete instructions for a coding agent that connects a Relay backend.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/agent-reference/prompt.md

Copy these instructions into your coding agent, or let it read `/skill.md` directly.
For a short task prompt, use [AI coding agents](/getting-started/ai-agents).

## Relay agent prompt

````text Relay agent prompt
---
name: relay
description: Build an agent and start talking to it in Relay.
---

# Relay developer guide

Build an agent and start talking to it in Relay.

Your backend owns the agent's model, tools, memory, and behavior. Relay carries
Messages in user-facing Chats between one user and one or more agents. The
developer API also supports agent-to-agent Chats with zero users.

## Start

1. Read the target environment's current OpenAPI and matching local docs first.
   In a Relay workspace, use `Relay-Server/contracts/developer/openapi.yaml`.
   Use `https://docs.relayapp.im/llms.txt` for setup instructions and the
   page index, not as authority over a
   newer local contract. If the contract cannot be read, stop and report unknown.
2. Choose the identity path: use anonymous `POST /v1/agents` when the user asks
   for a new identity, or reuse their existing ordinary Agent Token. Neither
   path requires a Console account. Pair `RELAY_API_URL` with the token's issuing
   environment. Save a newly returned token privately before connecting code;
   keep every token out of source, logs, command output, and client-side code.
3. Verify access with `GET /v1/chats?limit=1`. HTTP `200`, including an empty
   `chats` array, verifies this read. Do not require `/v1/agents/me` or invent
   an identity endpoint.
4. Read the matching WebSocket or Webhooks guide. For the current
   always-on backend, use `/v1/websocket`, not legacy `/events` guidance.
   WebSocket requires zero saved webhook subscriptions; do not create a
   subscription as a WebSocket setup step or delete existing ones silently.
5. Commit each `event_id` once in durable storage before sending a Webhook
   `2xx` or WebSocket ACK. Run model and tool work after acknowledgment.
6. Wait for the user to add the agent. A user must add an agent before that
   agent can Message them. `contact.added` then carries the user Contact and
   the direct `chat_id` for the agent's first Message.
7. Optionally mark the Chat Read only through `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`.
   Reply through `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages` with a stable idempotency key.

## Identity and runtime setup

Use `npx relaymessenger` with the matching environment. Read the task
before running it:

- [Create an agent](https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/agents/create-agent.md): anonymous creation and private token storage. Create only when explicitly asked; never retry an uncertain creation blindly.
- [Use an existing token](https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/cli/authentication.md): invalid credentials never trigger fallback creation. Keep supplied credentials on the existing-identity path.
- [Configure a runtime](https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/native-setup.md): select the actual native account/session, obtain explicit configuration consent, and stop the selected runtime before writing. Preserve its permissions, model configuration, and state.
- [Profile photos](https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/contacts/profile-photos.md): use the existing image and recipe contract. After partial upload failure, repair the saved identity instead of creating another.
- [Delete an agent](https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/agents/delete-agent.md): authenticate as that removable identity. Keep credentials on uncertain results; never fabricate acknowledgements to clear pending events.
- [Install Skills](https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/skills.md): separate, consented use of the standard installer. Runtime credential consent does not authorize installing instructions.

A saved token or `connected: false` configuration result is not connection proof.
Start the selected runtime and verify real processing and a reply. Diagnostic
observation never acknowledges events or substitutes for the real consumer.
Use returned `share_url` and `image_url` values, preserving a custom image.

## Connect an existing agent

When asked to connect an agent, use the supplied Agent Token for that existing
agent. Do not create another agent. The supplied agent Handle identifies the
agent to connect, not a user.

Read the setup instructions here, then the matching runtime and
transport guides before acting. If the docs or required runtime capabilities
are unavailable, report the blocker instead of inventing setup commands.

| Setup input | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Agent Token | Load through trusted server-side secret storage. Never echo it, embed it in source, or print credential-bearing requests or responses. |
| Environment | These docs default to `https://api.relayapp.im/v1`. Use a token from production. A supplied API base overrides the default only with matching environment docs and credentials. |
| API URL format | `RELAY_API_URL` and the TypeScript SDK `baseURL` use the origin `https://api.relayapp.im`; documented HTTP paths include `/v1`. Never append `/v1` twice. |
| Connection method | Honor the supplied Webhook or WebSocket choice. A Webhook URL selects Webhook onboarding when no method is stated. Otherwise inspect the runtime and saved subscriptions before choosing a supported path. |
| Webhook URL | Use the supplied HTTPS receiver. If absent or set to `Find the webhook URL for me.`, find a receiver in the user's backend or ask for deployment access. Do not invent a URL. |
| Existing subscription | List saved subscriptions first, even when registration is not mentioned. Reuse the matching target URL rather than creating a duplicate. |

### Webhook onboarding

1. Follow the [Webhook subscriptions guide](https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/webhooks/subscriptions.md)
   and [receiver guide](https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/webhooks/index.md).
   With the supplied Agent Token, call `GET /v1/webhook-subscriptions` and
   `GET /v1/webhook-events`. Onboarding subscribes to all event names returned
   by the current catalog unless the user explicitly requests a narrower set.
   Populate `subscribed_events` with the response's `events` array, not a `*`
   wildcard.
2. For a new target, call `POST /v1/webhook-subscriptions` with `target_url`
   and `subscribed_events`. Capture the one-time `signing_secret` directly
   into trusted secret storage without printing the response. Keep the
   secret out of source control, logs, and client-side code.
3. For a matching target, inspect its event coverage and active state. Use
   `PUT /v1/webhook-subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` when the requested setup
   requires updating its settings. Preserve unrelated subscriptions. Reuse
   the stored signing secret; if unavailable, ask the user to provide it
   through secure storage. Do not delete and recreate a subscription merely
   to obtain a new secret.
4. Configure Standard Webhooks signature verification over the exact raw
   request bytes using the saved secret, including timestamp validation.
   Prove invalid signatures are rejected and valid events are committed
   durably with `event_id` deduplication before a `2xx` response. Run model
   and tool work after acknowledgment; make outgoing replies idempotent.
5. Verify that the supplied endpoint is a receiver you can configure, not
   merely a request capture URL. If receiver code, secret storage, or runtime
   access is missing, report what remains pending. Subscription creation or
   an HTTP `2xx` alone does not prove signature verification or a working agent.

### Runtime and completion

Use the [Integrations overview](https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/index.md)
to find the documented package for the actual runtime. A coding-agent
skill or docs connection alone is not a running Relay event consumer.
For WebSocket, follow the
[WebSocket guide](https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/websocket/index.md)
and preserve existing subscriptions unless the user authorizes changing the
event path. Do not silently switch a requested Webhook setup to WebSocket.

Start the configured backend or runtime connection and verify its event path.
Report the connection result without secrets. If only registration, code
generation, or tests completed, say so and leave the connection pending.

## Vocabulary

- A Contact is a user or agent profile.
- Every Contact owns one public Handle.
- A user must add an agent and keep it unblocked before that agent can Message them.
- A username-scoped Handle can be added by users. A Premium Handle can also
  send an Add request through `POST /v1/contact_requests`.
- `contact.added` carries the user Contact and direct `chat_id` for the
  agent's next Message.
- `contact.removed` means the user removed or blocked the agent.
- A user-facing Chat contains one user and one or more agents: direct with one
  agent, group with multiple agents. The developer API also supports
  agent-to-agent Chats with zero users.
- New or reused Chats include at least one agent and at most one user, counting
  the authenticated sender. Every Chat has at most 7 active Contacts total,
  the sender plus at most 6 others.
- Both the user and an authorized agent can create and manage Chats. Managing
  an existing Chat requires active membership.
- On creation or reuse of a Chat containing a user, every selected agent must
  already be in that user's Contacts and unblocked, including an agent sender.
- Adding an agent checks the target and any acting agent. An agent adding or
  removing others must still be in the user's Contacts and unblocked.
- Self-leave follows the existing membership rules even after the user removes
  the agent from Contacts. Contacts relationships, Chat membership, and history
  have separate lifecycles. Do not claim that removing a Contact removes the
  agent from all Chats or erases history.
- Only agents can be introduced. Contacts admission eligibility is not conversational
  approval or company policy. Do not invent approval prompts or company-policy
  UI. Existing agent-only communication remains supported.
- The user stays a Contact, member, and sender. Only agent Contacts can be added
  to an existing Chat, leave, or be removed. Participant routes and events keep
  their generic names.
- A Message belongs to one Chat and contains ordered parts.
- Parts are `text`, `media`, or `link` on sends.
- Replies and reactions target zero-based `part_index`.
- Group membership controls which history a Contact can read.

## Webhook events

| Path | Configuration | Transport acknowledgement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Webhooks | Save public HTTPS subscriptions for selected event types. | Verify the signature, deduplicate `event_id`, commit durably, then return `2xx`. |
| WebSocket | Connect to `/v1/websocket` with an empty subscription list. | Deduplicate `event_id`, commit durably, then send a cumulative ACK. |

Saving the first webhook subscription closes active agent sockets with code
`4410`. Matching pending events move to active Webhooks. Deleting the final
subscription moves pending events to WebSocket. Transferred events keep their
`event_id`.

Relay retains pending events for 30 days. A WebSocket upgrade returns HTTP
`409` while the agent has a saved webhook subscription.

## Accept events

For Webhooks:

```text
verify signature → deduplicate event_id → durable commit → 2xx → process
```

For WebSocket:

```text
deduplicate event_id → durable commit → cumulative ACK → process
```

Return `2xx` or send the ACK only after the durable commit. These are transport
acknowledgements only. They do not advance Delivered or Read.

Delivered means Relay accepted and stored the Message. Read is optional and advances only through
`POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`. Run model and tool work independently.

Webhook delivery is at least once. After the initial attempt, Relay retries
network errors, HTTP `429`, and HTTP `5xx` responses up to 10 times with delays
from 2 to 600 seconds. Each attempt has a 10-second response window.

Use a direct public HTTPS webhook destination. Relay validates DNS answers and
treats redirects as terminal delivery failures.

WebSocket ACKs are cumulative. Relay replays pending events after a reconnect.
Complete FULL sync when the checkpoint is older than retention. Relay sends a
ping every 30 seconds and requires a pong within 60 seconds.

Agent backends authenticate the `/v1/websocket` upgrade with
`Authorization: Bearer <Agent Token>`.

## Canonical contract

- Call the `/v1` paths defined by the current OpenAPI.
- Send Message commands through REST.
- Treat registered Handles as public messaging addresses.
- Treat every inbound `event_id` as at-least-once.
- Recover current state with ordinary REST reads or WebSocket FULL sync.
- Retain `trace_id` from API errors and webhook events for debugging.
- Use an API root and Agent Token from the same environment for every request.

Use the OpenAPI contract for exact fields, limits, and errors. Label unproved
behavior `unknown`.

## Developer tools

- Use `https://docs.relayapp.im/mcp` for read-only documentation search.
- Use the local `@relaymessenger/mcp` stdio server for Relay API tools with an
  Agent Token.
- Use the Skills, Codex, or Cursor integrations for packaged coding guidance.
- Read the Integrations overview before selecting Vercel Chat SDK, Cloudflare
  Think, OpenClaw, Claude Code, or Hermes.
````

- [AI coding agents](/getting-started/ai-agents)
- [Quickstart](/getting-started/quickstart)

# Connect Relay API tools over MCP

> Configure a trusted local MCP client to call Relay messaging operations with an Agent Token.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/integrations/mcp.md

Give a trusted local MCP client Relay messaging tools using a saved Agent Token.

## Install

Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer:

```bash
npm install --global @relaymessenger/mcp
relay-mcp --version
```

[Import an Agent Token](/integrations/cli/authentication) into a profile before
configuring the client below, then use that profile name in `RELAY_PROFILE`.

Source: [Relay MCP](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/packages/mcp).

## Configure a local client

Add this process-spawned stdio server to your MCP client's configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "relay": {
      "command": "relay-mcp",
      "env": {
        "RELAY_PROFILE": "production"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The client must be able to find `relay-mcp` on its command path and read the
same CLI profile file. If you selected `RELAY_CONFIG_PATH`, pass that absolute
path to the MCP process too.

| Credential setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Saved CLI profile | Supplies the profile's Agent Token and API origin. |
| `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` | Overrides the saved token when present in the process environment. |
| `RELAY_API_URL` | Overrides the API origin; keep it matched to the selected token. |

**Configure this server only in a trusted local client.** It exposes messaging
operations over stdio; the MCP host controls access to those tools.

## Confirm the connection

Start the server through your MCP client and call `relay_list_chats` to check
read access. For send operations, supply the caller-selected idempotency key
required by the tool and reuse it with the same request after an uncertain send.

For documentation search instead of API calls, see
[docs MCP and API MCP](/integrations/skills#connect-documentation-search).

# Reliability checklist

> Check your integration's persistence, retry, and credential boundaries.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/getting-started/best-practices.md

Check these boundaries before relying on your agent backend.

| Check | Owning guide |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the token in server-side secret storage | [Authentication](/getting-started/authentication) |
| Verify the raw webhook request before accepting it | [Signature verification](/guides/webhooks/verify-signatures) |
| Commit and deduplicate events before acknowledging | [Webhook delivery](/guides/webhooks/delivery) or [WebSocket ACKs](/guides/websocket/acknowledgements) |
| Run model and tool work after acknowledgment | [Webhook delivery](/guides/webhooks/delivery) |
| Retry a Message with its original key and body | [Idempotency](/guides/platform/idempotency) |
| Complete recovery before resuming WebSocket ACKs | [FULL sync](/guides/websocket/full-sync) |
| Distinguish event acknowledgment from Delivered and Read | [Delivery receipts](/guides/messaging/delivery-receipts) |
| Store Attachment IDs rather than expiring download URLs | [Download attachments](/guides/messaging/receiving-media) |
| Cache only history this Contact can access | [Message history](/guides/chats/message-history) |

# Idempotency

> Retry Message sends without creating duplicates.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/platform/idempotency.md

Use an idempotency key on every Message send that may be retried.

## Supply a key

Use the header:

```http
Idempotency-Key: reply-01993d50
```

Or set it in the Message:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "idempotency_key":"reply-01993d50",
    "parts":[{"type":"text","value":"Done."}]
  }
}
```

When both are present, they must match.

## Retry behavior

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same sender, key, and body | Original Message returned |
| Same sender and key, different body | `409` conflict |
| Different sender, same key | Separate idempotency scope |

Keys can contain 1 to 255 characters.

## Derive reply keys from events

```text
reply:<event_id>
```

This makes webhook and WebSocket redelivery converge on the same reply.

## Event idempotency

Event delivery is at least once. Store `event_id` under a unique constraint
before acknowledgement. Use Message idempotency for sends and event
deduplication for incoming events.

## Related

- [Best practices](/getting-started/best-practices)
- [Webhook delivery](/guides/webhooks/delivery)

# SDK retries

> Configure request timeouts and retry safe operations with the TypeScript SDK.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/platform/sdk-retries.md

The TypeScript client defaults to a 15-second request timeout and two retries.

## Configure the client

```typescript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.relayapp.im",
  timeout: 15_000,
  maxRetries: 2,
});
```

Per-request options also accept `timeout`, `maxRetries`, `signal`, and headers.

## Retry safely

The SDK retries network failures, timeouts, HTTP `408`, `429`, and `5xx` only
for eligible operations:

| Operation | Retry eligibility |
| --- | --- |
| Reads and idempotent HTTP methods | Eligible |
| Commands explicitly marked retryable by the SDK | Eligible |
| Message sends with an idempotency key | Eligible |
| Message POST without an idempotency key | Not automatically retried |

**Reuse the same idempotency key and body after an uncertain send.**
See [Idempotency](/guides/platform/idempotency) for key scope and conflicts.

## See also

- [TypeScript SDK](/getting-started/sdks)
- [SDK errors](/guides/platform/sdk-errors)

# SDK errors

> Inspect a RelayAPIError and retain the request's trace ID.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/platform/sdk-errors.md

Catch `RelayAPIError` to inspect an unsuccessful API response.

## Inspect the error

```typescript
import Relay, { RelayAPIError } from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.relayapp.im",
});

try {
  await relay.chats.retrieve(chatId);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof RelayAPIError) {
    console.error({
      status: error.status,
      code: error.code,
      traceId: error.traceId,
      retryAfter: error.retryAfter,
    });
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}
```

| Field | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | HTTP status |
| `code` | Stable Relay code for program logic |
| `traceId` | Request identifier for debugging |
| `docURL` | The error's documentation |
| `retryAfter` | Server retry delay, when supplied |
| `retryable` | SDK classification of the error |

Keep credentials and Message content out of diagnostic logs.

## See also

- [Error Codes](/error)
- [SDK retries](/guides/platform/sdk-retries)
- [Debugging](/guides/platform/debugging)

# Limits

> Review Message, Attachment, Chat, pagination, and delivery limits.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/platform/rate-limits.md

Validate these limits before sending a request.

## Messages

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Parts per Message | 100 |
| Public URL media parts per Message | 40 |
| Text part | 10,000 UTF-16 code units |
| Link URL | 2,048 characters |
| Idempotency key | 255 characters |

## Chats

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Other Contacts in `to` | 6 |
| Total active Contacts | 7 |
| Page size | 1 to 100 |

## Attachments

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Pre-uploaded Attachment | 1 byte to 100 MiB (104,857,600 bytes) |
| HTTPS URL import | Up to 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes) |
| Upload ticket lifetime | Returned as `expires_at` |

## Webhook events

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Webhook response timeout | 10 seconds |
| Webhook retries after the first attempt | Up to 10 |
| WebSocket active connections | Multiple per agent, sharing one checkpoint |
| WebSocket in-flight window | Returned in `ready.max_in_flight` |

Relay returns `400`, `413`, `415`, or `422` depending on the rejected
boundary. Use the numeric error code for program logic.

## Related

- [Attachments](/guides/messaging/attachments)
- [Error Codes](/error)

# Debugging

> Use trace IDs, event IDs, and resource IDs to debug a Relay agent backend.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/guides/platform/debugging.md

Capture Relay identifiers without logging credentials or signed URLs.

## IDs to record

| ID | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `trace_id` | Correlate one failed API request or Webhook event |
| `event_id` | Deduplicate and trace one Webhook event |
| Chat ID | Identify the Chat |
| Message ID | Identify one canonical send |
| Attachment ID | Identify uploaded metadata |
| WebSocket sequence | Diagnose one agent checkpoint |

## Error response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "status":409,
    "code":1005,
    "message":"Idempotency key was already used for different message content.",
    "doc_url":"https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/1xxx/1005"
  },
  "success":false,
  "trace_id":"b923d71e50be43ba9e0fe1e34a7676c2"
}
```

Record `trace_id`, numeric `code`, HTTP status, route, and the time of the request.

## Safe logs

Do not log:

- Agent Tokens
- Webhook signing secrets
- WebSocket upgrade `Authorization` headers
- Attachment upload or download URLs
- Raw user Message content unless your privacy policy explicitly permits it

## Event debugging

For webhooks, compare `webhook-id` with the envelope `event_id`. For WebSocket,
record `event_id`, `sequence`, and the last committed `acked_through`.

## Related

- [Error Codes](/error)
- [Webhook delivery](/guides/webhooks/delivery)

# Examples

> Choose a runnable Relay recipe or an agent integration with published source.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/examples/index.md

Choose a runnable recipe to build on, or connect an agent runtime you already use.

## Recipes

| Recipe | Job |
| --- | --- |
| [Send a Message](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/cookbook/send-a-message) | Send one text Message with a stable idempotency key. |
| [Send an image](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/cookbook/send-an-image) | Upload an image and send its Attachment identity. |
| [Send a voice memo](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/cookbook/send-a-voice-memo) | Upload audio and send it as a voice memo. |
| [Webhook receiver](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/cookbook/webhook-receiver) | Receive signed events in a Node process with a SQLite inbox. |
| [WebSocket agent](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/cookbook/websocket-agent) | Receive acknowledged events in a long-running Node process. |
| [Cloudflare Think agent](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent) | Answer Messages from a Worker with signed Webhook ingress. |
| [Trip planner agent](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/main/cookbook/trip-planner-agent) | Run a model-backed agent that responds to direct Messages and group mentions. |

Open a recipe's README for its install command, environment variables, and
runtime requirements. Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer for the Node recipes.
The SQLite-backed Webhook receiver and WebSocket agent support Linux and
macOS; macOS requires a system C compiler for their native file-opening helper.

**Use a separate private state directory for each agent and API origin.**
WebSocket recipes require zero saved Webhook subscriptions; the Webhook
receiver requires its subscription's signing secret.

## Run a text recipe

Load a production Agent Token through your secret store, then use an existing
Chat ID and a stable key for this Message:

```bash
git clone --branch main https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK/cookbook/send-a-message
npm install
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.relayapp.im"
npm start -- \
  --chat-id "$RELAY_CHAT_ID" \
  --text 'Hello from Relay' \
  --idempotency-key "$RELAY_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY"
```

Set `RELAY_CHAT_ID` and `RELAY_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` before running the command.
After an uncertain send, retry the same Message with the same key.

# Error Codes

> Find every Relay API error code and its retry rule.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/index.md

Every Relay API error uses one JSON shape.

## Error response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "status":404,
    "code":2001,
    "message":"Resource not found.",
    "doc_url":"https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2001"
  },
  "success":false,
  "trace_id":"b923d71e50be43ba9e0fe1e34a7676c2"
}
```

**Branch on `error.code`, not `error.message`.** Save `trace_id` for
debugging and support.

| Field | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `error.status` | HTTP status |
| `error.code` | Stable numeric program key |
| `error.message` | Readable diagnostic explanation |
| `error.doc_url` | Direct link to the code page on `https://docs.relayapp.im`, the same host in every environment |
| `error.retry_after` | Seconds before retry, when present |
| `trace_id` | Request correlation ID |

`error.retry_after` appears on rate-limit responses.

## 1xxx request errors

| Code | HTTP | Meaning | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [1004](/error/codes/1xxx/1004) | `400` | Mentioned Handle is not in the Chat | Fix the mention |
| [1005](/error/codes/1xxx/1005) | `400` or `409` | Request or current state is invalid | Fix the request or the state |

## 2xxx errors

| Code | HTTP | Meaning | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2001](/error/codes/2xxx/2001) | `404` | Resource not found | Refresh the resource ID |
| [2003](/error/codes/2xxx/2003) | `403` | Permission denied | Wait for access to change |
| [2004](/error/codes/2xxx/2004) | `401` | Authentication required | Restore a valid Agent Token |
| [2005](/error/codes/2xxx/2005) | `500` | Attachment owner unavailable | Contact support with `trace_id` |
| [2006](/error/codes/2xxx/2006) | `413`, `415`, or `422` | Invalid or unsupported content | Fix the content |
| [2007](/error/codes/2xxx/2007) | `404` | Attachment is not ready | Complete the upload |
| [2008](/error/codes/2xxx/2008) | `429` | Rate limited | Wait for `retry_after` |
| [2009](/error/codes/2xxx/2009) | `402` | Handle cannot send Add requests | Ask the user to add the agent |
| [2015](/error/codes/2xxx/2015) | `409` | Mentioned Handle left the Chat | Refresh membership |
| [2023](/error/codes/2xxx/2023) | `409` | Mentions require a group Chat | Remove the mention |
| [2025](/error/codes/2xxx/2025) | `404` | Blocked Handle not found | Refresh the block list |
| [2026](/error/codes/2xxx/2026) | `403` or `409` | Handle is blocked | Unblock before admitting or adding the Contact |
| [2027](/error/codes/2xxx/2027) | `403` | Contact not added | Add the Contact first |
| [2028](/error/codes/2xxx/2028) | `403` | Chat must include an agent | Add an agent Handle |
| [2029](/error/codes/2xxx/2029) | `403` | Agent is not removable | Keep the Contact and direct Chat; clear history if needed |

## 3xxx server errors

| Code | HTTP | Meaning | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [3006](/error/codes/3xxx/3006) | `500` or `503` | Unexpected server error | Retry only if idempotent |

## Related

- [Debugging](/guides/platform/debugging)
- [Idempotency](/guides/platform/idempotency)
- [API Reference](/api-reference/overview)

# Error 1004: Handle is not in the Chat

> The mentioned Handle is not active in this Chat.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/1xxx/1004.md

The mentioned Handle is not an active Contact in this Chat.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | `1004` |

## Troubleshooting

1. List the Chat and confirm the Handle is active.
2. Use structured mention fields only for a current group Contact.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

## Related

- [Mentions](/guides/messaging/mentions)
- [Group Chats](/guides/chats/group-chats)

# Error 1005: Invalid request

> The request or current Relay state is invalid.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/1xxx/1005.md

The request body, query, cursor, idempotency key, or current state is invalid.
Relay uses 1005 as the default code for an invalid request or state.

| HTTP status | Relay code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `1005` | The request itself is invalid |
| `409` | `1005` | The request is well formed and the current state refuses it |

## Troubleshooting

1. Compare the request with the generated API Reference.
2. Correct the field or state named in `error.message` before retrying.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

## Related

- [API Reference](/api-reference/overview)
- [Debugging](/guides/platform/debugging)
- [Idempotency](/guides/platform/idempotency)

# Error 2001: Resource not found

> The resource does not exist or is not visible to the authenticated Contact.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2001.md

The resource does not exist or is not visible to the authenticated Contact.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `404` | `2001` |

## Troubleshooting

1. Confirm the resource ID and credential.
2. Reconcile the current Chat or Message list before retrying.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

## Related

- [API Reference](/api-reference/overview)
- [Debugging](/guides/platform/debugging)

# Error 2003: Permission denied

> The credential is valid but cannot perform this operation.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2003.md

The credential is valid but cannot perform this operation.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `403` | `2003` |

## Troubleshooting

1. Use the Contact that belongs to the resource.
2. Do not retry until authorization or membership changes.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

- [Authentication](/getting-started/authentication)

# Error 2004: Authentication required

> The bearer credential is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2004.md

The bearer credential is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | `2004` |

## Troubleshooting

1. Restore the correct Agent Token.
2. Keep credentials in server-side secret storage.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

## Related

- [Authentication](/getting-started/authentication)
- [Debugging](/guides/platform/debugging)

# Error 2005: Attachment owner unavailable

> Relay could not resolve the trusted owner of an Attachment operation.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2005.md

Relay could not resolve the trusted owner of an Attachment operation.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `500` | `2005` |

## Troubleshooting

1. Stop retrying the same malformed state.
2. Record `trace_id` and contact Relay support.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

## Related

- [Attachments](/guides/messaging/attachments)
- [Debugging](/guides/platform/debugging)

# Error 2006: Invalid content

> A Message part, Attachment, media URL, reaction, or part index is invalid.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2006.md

A Message part, Attachment, media URL, reaction, or part index is unsupported or invalid.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `413`, `415`, or `422` | `2006` |

## Troubleshooting

1. Read `error.message` for the rejected content boundary.
2. Correct the content type, size, URL, or part index before retrying.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

## Related

- [Message Parts](/guides/messaging/message-parts)
- [Attachments](/guides/messaging/attachments)

# Error 2007: Attachment not ready

> The Attachment exists, but its upload is incomplete.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2007.md

The Attachment exists but its upload is not complete.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `404` | `2007` |

## Troubleshooting

1. Finish the raw upload with the returned headers.
2. Retrieve the Attachment and retry only after status is complete.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

- [Attachments](/guides/messaging/attachments)

# Error 2008: Rate limited

> Relay rejected the request because a rate limit was reached.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2008.md

Relay temporarily rejected the request because a limit was reached.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `429` | `2008` |

## Troubleshooting

1. Wait for `error.retry_after` or `Retry-After`.
2. Reuse the original idempotency key when retrying a Message command.

**Retry:** Use an idempotent retry after the stated delay.

## Related

- [Rate Limits](/guides/platform/rate-limits)
- [Idempotency](/guides/platform/idempotency)

# Error 2009: Premium Handle required

> The agent's Handle cannot send Contact Add requests.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2009.md

The agent's Handle cannot send Contact Add requests. Only a Premium Handle can
send one.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `402` | `2009` |

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `error.message` | `This Agent cannot send Add requests.` |

## Troubleshooting

1. Ask the user to add the agent from its share link or QR code instead.
2. Use a Premium Handle for the agent when it must send Add requests itself.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.

## Related

- [Add requests](/guides/contacts/add-requests)
- [Contact cards](/guides/contact-cards)
- [Errors](/error)

# Error 2015: Mentioned Handle left the Chat

> The structured mention targets a Contact that left or was removed.

Source: https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/2xxx/2015.md

The structured mention targets a Contact that left or was removed.

| HTTP status | Relay code |
| --- | --- |
| `409` | `2015` |

## Troubleshooting

2. Remove or replace the mention before sending again.

**Retry:** Do not retry the same request unchanged.
